question.text: Yamuna Capital AIF values investee Bharat Metals on NAV basis. Equity share capital = INR 2 crore; General reserve = INR 10 crore; Revaluation reserve = INR 3 crore; Capital Redemption Reserve = INR 5 crore; P&L surplus = INR 4 crore. Number of shares = 20 lakh. What is the book NAV per share (cash net worth basis per PDF Illustration 11.4)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Cash net worth excludes the revaluation reserve. Tangible NAV = Equity capital + General reserve + Capital Redemption Reserve + P&L surplus = 2 + 10 + 5 + 4 = INR 21 crore. NAV per share = 21,00,00,000 / 20,00,000 = INR 105. The Trap: INR 120 incorrectly includes the revaluation reserve. INR 100 wrongly excludes both the revaluation reserve and the Capital Redemption Reserve. INR 115 mistreats the Capital Redemption Reserve. Note: The workbook supports NAV per share as equity shareholders' funds divided by paid-up equity shares, with revaluation reserve excluded from cash net worth per the Illustration 11.4 footnote.
